config.fills: Buy at ask, sell at bid, same labelled hourly bar; not guaranteed executable ticks.
config.long_rule: Choose closest strike to 70% of first Monday spot, among 60%-80% on $5 grid; ties lower strike. Entry quotes only.
config.short_rule: Monday 11 ET; lowest eligible $5 strike >= 103% spot among first three candidates; strike exceeds long strike.
config.exit_rule: Buy short back Friday 15 ET, or first 15 ET observation with ITM short and <= $0.05 mid extrinsic. No new call that week.
config.missing_exit: Halt at first unavailable mandatory exit. Never discard a filled trade using future liquidity.
config.dividends: AMZN has never paid cash dividends per Amazon IR FAQ; no dividends assumed in this sample.
config.selection_disclosure: Stock and parameters selected retrospectively for an educational case study, not an out-of-sample investment claim.

provenance.source_kind: actual API responses, not modelled prices

funding.note: Initial net booked outlay, including any first-Monday call premium and fees. Capital saving does not imply equal risk; all results use identical starting cash. Remaining cash is reserved; no broker margin entitlement is assumed.

scenarios.name: Immediate assignment and voluntary long exercise at first short entry
scenarios.assumption: Mechanical off-path stress, including possible voluntary assignment while OTM; not a claim of observed assignment. Assignment first creates 100 short shares. Long exercise is an explicit election, not automatic. Both settle together in this scenario; broker permission, settlement timing, borrow and exercise fees are not modelled.

methodology.fills: Buy at ask; sell at bid; option fee per contract on every leg. Quotes are same-label hourly observations, not guaranteed simultaneous or executable ticks.
methodology.marks: Contemporaneous bid/ask mid; liquidation NAV uses bid for longs, ask for shorts and includes option close fees. Missing quotes produce gaps, never forward-filled.
methodology.capital: Four independent $50,000 accounts; no borrowing. PMCC is a debit diagonal spread, not stock-covered. No portfolio-margin or stock-covered Reg T assumption.
methodology.assignment: Base path assumes no early assignment before rule-based close. Daily checks cannot eliminate overnight or intraday American-option assignment risk. Separate explicit assignment/exercise stress.
methodology.benchmark: Same-call-schedule covered call holds 100 shares and uses the PMCC short trades. Buy-and-hold and long-call-only enter and exit on the same horizon. Common initial cash, no interest or dividends.
methodology.selection: Fixed stock, dates and rules are a retrospective case study; entry decisions never use later quote availability or realized returns.
methodology.metrics: No annualization. Observed-NAV drawdown may understate true drawdown where marks are missing. Daily returns only use complete adjacent weekdays (Friday to Monday allowed); holiday bridges are excluded.

last_common_mark.note: Last simultaneous complete mark for comparison only. This does not book liquidation or replace an unresolved final quote.

scatter.caveat: Bar last-trade prints need not be contemporaneous with bar bid/ask and may be stale. R² is diagnostic, not proof that a mid fill is executable; the backtest pays the displayed spread.

execution_sensitivity.name: $0.01 adverse option fill per share
execution_sensitivity.assumption: Fixed booked trade schedule; option buys pay this much above ask and sells receive this much below bid, floored at zero. A cost attribution, not a rerun of eligibility or a guarantee that stressed trades remain fundable.

execution_sensitivity.name: $0.05 adverse option fill per share
execution_sensitivity.assumption: Fixed booked trade schedule; option buys pay this much above ask and sells receive this much below bid, floored at zero. A cost attribution, not a rerun of eligibility or a guarantee that stressed trades remain fundable.

limitations: Candidate strikes are a fixed sampled grid, not an independently reconstructed historical full option chain.
API errors and empty responses are data-availability failures, not evidence that the market did not trade.
Source timestamps are hourly end labels. Neither synchronized tick quotes nor actual executable orders are observed.
Acquisition may use current symbology aliases to retrieve old observations; decisions use only the entry-time quotes.
Base case does not model stochastic early assignment, borrow or financing; explicit daily risk checks and separate stress make this limitation visible.
